item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00050","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C24","C12","C03"],"selected_candidate_label":"C24","confidence":0.84,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C24 is a plausible immediate drafting template. It uses the same distinctive opening—“it is hereby ordered, in the interest of the internal management of the Government, as follows”—and the same basic machinery of a short numbered order assigning functions under a newly enacted statute to designated executive agencies. The child adapts that framework by authorizing the Economic Cooperation Administrator to allocate funds and by making a statutory determination permitting specified legal exemptions. C12 and C03 share agency-delegation machinery but lack the child's unusually close framing and compact structure.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"it is hereby ordered, in the interest of the internal management of the Government, as follows:","parent_excerpt":"it is hereby ordered, in the interest of the internal management of the Government, as follows:","explanation":"Exact and relatively distinctive introductory formula shared by directives issued eight days apart."},{"child_excerpt":"The Administrator for Economic Cooperation is hereby authorized and directed to make appropriate allocations, for the purposes of Titles I and IV of the Act","parent_excerpt":"The Secretary of Commerce shall perform and exercise the functions, duties, powers, authority, and discretion ... vested in the President by sections 3, 4, 18(c), and 18(d) of the Rubber Act of 1948.","explanation":"Both begin their operative provisions by assigning statutory implementation authority to a named executive official."},{"child_excerpt":"It is hereby determined, pursuant to sections 119 and 403 of the Act, that the performance of the functions authorized under Titles I and IV of the Act without regard to the following laws will further the purposes of the said Titles I and IV","parent_excerpt":"The Reconstruction Finance Corporation shall perform and exercise the functions vested in the President by, or designated in, sections 5(c), 5(e), 6, 7, 8, 11(a), and 18(f) of the Rubber Act of 1948","explanation":"Each proceeds through compact numbered provisions keyed to specific statutory sections, adapting the same administrative implementation framework to a different act."}]}
